title: Fix Open DXF Contours for Laser Cutting | Cut It Out
description: DXF showing an open contour error? Find gaps in your outline, check repair options in File Workshop and make sure the shape is right before ordering.
heading:
A gap in your DXF?
Here’s how to check it.
heading_text: A gap in your DXF? Here’s how to check it
intro: An ‘open contour’ is an outline with a gap. The lines around your part or a hole do not quite meet. This guide helps you find the gap and decide how to fix it.

title: Remove Duplicate DXF Lines for Laser Cutting | Cut It Out
description: DXF showing duplicate lines? Learn why overlapping lines are hard to spot and how to check and remove extra copies without changing your part.
heading:
Duplicate lines in your DXF?
Remove the extra copies.
heading_text: Duplicate lines in your DXF? Remove the extra copies
intro: A duplicate line is an extra copy of a line already in your drawing. The copies sit on top of each other, so they can be hard to spot. Here’s how to check them without removing a line your part needs.

title: DXF Scale Problems: Check Inches, mm & Size | Cut It Out
description: DXF too big or too small? Check the units, compare the correct size with the size shown and use our calculator to work out the scale change.
heading:
DXF the wrong size?
Check it before you order.
heading_text: DXF the wrong size? Check it before you order
intro: Your drawing can look right but upload too big or too small. Start with a measurement you know, such as the overall width, and compare it with the size shown after uploading.

title: STEP vs DXF for Laser Cutting: Which File? | Cut It Out
description: Not sure whether to upload DXF or STEP? Compare a flat 2D drawing with a 3D sheet-metal model and find the right starting point for your laser cutting quote.
heading:
DXF or STEP?
Which file should you upload?
heading_text: DXF or STEP? Which file should you upload?
intro: DXF is a flat 2D drawing of the shape to cut. STEP is a 3D model. We can use suitable sheet-metal STEP models too, but all parts are cut and supplied flat. Here’s how to choose your file.
